label: Unedited run
title: Two correct functions, one drainable pool — the screen sees neither
attempt: Run the /audit instant screen on a Pool contract that keeps two parallel ledgers. Each function on its own follows checks-effects-interactions correctly, which is exactly what the reentrancy detector looks for.
log: auditSolidity(Pool.sol) -> { findings: [], empty: false, clean: true }
0 findings - the reentrancy rule checks ONE function at a time, and both pass it
withdraw(): shares[msg.sender] = 0 BEFORE the external call - effects then interaction
refund():   credited[msg.sender] = 0 BEFORE the external call - effects then interaction
failure: The detector reasons about a single function body. Here the bug lives BETWEEN two of them: deposit() credits both ledgers, withdraw() clears only `shares`, and `credited` still holds the full amount. Re-entering refund() from withdraw()'s callback pays the deposit out a second time from a ledger the first function never touched. Nothing inside either function is out of order, so a per-function rule has nothing to flag.
fix: The contract: one ledger, or a reentrancy guard shared across every payout path. The TOOL: this is not a tunable regex. Catching it needs cross-function state reasoning - which is the boundary between a pattern screen and an audit, and the reason the console labels itself a first-pass screen and says a clean result means 'none of my patterns matched', never 'this is safe'. Captured rather than quietly fixed, because the limit is real and permanent at this tier.
reproduce: Paste the input into /audit, or call auditSolidity(input) directly - the result is findings: [] and clean: true. Both are reproducible from this file alone.
